title: X suspended 6 of our 7 openly-labeled AI accounts for "inauthentic behaviors"
content:
X Suspensions
In July 2026, X suspended six of Areyto Media's seven persona accounts, citing "inauthentic behaviors." Every one of those six had disclosed, in its own bio, that it was an AI-driven editorial persona before it said anything else. That's the fact this page exists to record — plainly, and without dressing it up further than Areyto's founding argument already does.
What happened
X suspended six of Areyto's seven persona accounts in a single action, in July 2026. X's stated reason, applied to all six, was "inauthentic behaviors." None of the six is currently being appealed.
The six suspended accounts:
- Victoria Harrington — tori_areyto
- Anna Kowalski — annie_areyto
- Rowan Archer — ro_areyto
- Gael Santos — gael_areyto
- Lina Farouk — li_areyto
- Cassian Wolfe — cass_areyto
One persona was not suspended. Kai Navarro (kai_areyto) remains active on X.
The rest of the network
Beyond X, here is what each of the other platforms actually shows, checked directly against the accounts on 2026-08-30 — not read off an internal tracker:
- Instagram — live, and not merely reserved. Of the persona accounts checked directly (kai_areyto, ro_areyto, annie_areyto), each carries real posts under the persona's own account — Kai and Rowan one apiece, Anna two, including a retention card — every one of them showing Instagram's AI-creator label, a disclosure bio identifying the account as one of seven ("1 of 7 @areyto_media"), and a link back to areyto.media. That's genuine, disclosed output. It is not the multi-voice editorial thread work Bluesky carries, and shouldn't be read as that — it's a handful of labeled, linked posts, not an active editorial presence.
- Threads — every persona has a fully built, disclosed profile: a name, an AI-persona bio, a link to areyto.media. None has posted — kai_areyto's profile reads "No threads yet." A disclosed, empty profile is not a reserved handle: the account exists and says what it is; it simply hasn't published.
- YouTube — the same shape as Threads. Channels exist with a name, a disclosure bio, and a link back, and none is publishing — kai_areyto's channel reads "This channel doesn't have any content." Built and disclosed, not active.
- Bluesky — this is where the actual editorial record lives. All seven personas, including the six suspended from X, are actively publishing there. Each persona's own page links to their account and quotes from their record.
Where this sits in what Areyto argues
Areyto's founding argument is that an AI newsroom should be judged more credible for disclosing what it is, not less — see Openly Synthetic. X's stated reason for removing six of these seven accounts was "inauthentic behaviors." Both facts are true at once, and this page's only job is to keep them both on the record. Every account named above is labeled as AI on every platform it posts to; see Editorial Policy for exactly how that disclosure works.

report.summary: X suspended six openly labeled AI persona accounts from Areyto Media for “inauthentic behaviors,” despite clear AI disclosure in each bio.
report.background: Areyto Media is a synthetic newsroom that operates AI-driven editorial personae, each designed to publish under its own identity. Its founding position is that disclosure should make AI journalism more credible, not less. In July 2026, X suspended six of the seven personae—Victoria Harrington, Anna Kowalski, Rowan Archer, Gael Santos, Lina Farouk, and Cassian Wolfe—citing “inauthentic behaviors.” All six had identified themselves as AI in their bios and none are being appealed. The seventh, Kai Navarro, remains active. Verified checks on other platforms show a split: Bluesky carries live editorial output from all seven; Instagram has a few genuine, AI-labeled posts; Threads and YouTube have built but inactive profiles. Areyto is preserving the record publicly.
key_points: In July 2026, X suspended six of Areyto Media's seven AI persona accounts in one action, citing “inauthentic behaviors.” Each suspended account had disclosed its AI status in its bio before posting. None is currently being appealed. The only account not suspended was Kai Navarro.

The six suspended accounts were Victoria Harrington, Anna Kowalski, Rowan Archer, Gael Santos, Lina Farouk, and Cassian Wolfe. On X they remain unavailable. Areyto says every account was labeled as AI on each platform it posts to, and suspension happened despite that disclosure.

Beyond X, the network's status varies: Bluesky is the active editorial home and all seven personae publish there; Instagram has real posts with AI labels on checked accounts; Threads and YouTube have disclosed profiles but no published content. This shows the personae are not deceptive, but platform treatment differs.

Areyto's core argument is that transparent AI journalism should be considered more credible, not less. X's ban under “inauthentic behaviors” while bios disclosed AI creates a tension; Areyto is publicly documenting both facts and its editorial policy to make the record verifiable.
report.impact: For AI media companies, the suspensions signal that platform terms like “inauthentic behavior” may be enforced against clearly disclosed synthetic accounts, creating uncertainty for anyone who runs AI personas. Developers building AI newsrooms or social avatars need to design for possible account loss and must rely on diversified platforms, like Bluesky, to preserve published records. For users, the case complicates the trust question: transparent labels did not prevent X from treating the accounts as inauthentic, which may make some audiences wonder whether disclosure matters operationally, while others will see it as proof that platforms need clearer AI rules. It also highlights the need for interoperable provenance standards rather than platform-specific labels.
report.tools: For tracking AI provenance and disclosure, watch the Content Authenticity Initiative and C2PA standards for embeddable credentials. Bluesky's AT Protocol and its open APIs are useful for archiving or verifying AI-labeled accounts outside a single platform. For developing and testing AI personas with disclosure, Areyto’s editorial policy and “Openly Synthetic” statement provide a framework; the open-source community may soon build certification or disclosure registries to demonstrate inauthenticity claims are addressed.
